obligation: Bank recall request for a diverted payment
trigger: A payment (ACH or wire) is suspected to have gone to an account controlled by an attacker
deadline: Immediately on suspicion. IC3: 'time is of the essence'
notify: The company's bank fraud desk (outbound payments); the owner calls its own bank (inbound payments)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - practical step, not a legal duty. First action in the BEC runbook
owner: Controller; Project Executive for owner payments

obligation: Complaint to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
trigger: Any business email compromise with a fraudulent transfer or attempt
deadline: As soon as possible, regardless of the amount; POL-03 requires the same day
notify: IC3 (www.ic3.gov); local FBI field office for large losses
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but required by company policy

obligation: Cyber insurance notice
trigger: Suspected security incident or funds transfer fraud
deadline: Before engaging incident vendors; social engineering claims need prompt notice and proof that verification was followed
notify: Carrier breach hotline ($10 million limit; $1 million social engineering sublimit; $250,000 retention)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not a legal duty

obligation: Review for evidence of compromise of covered defense information
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident affecting a covered contractor information system or the CDI in it, including CUI copied to an unauthorized system (definition of 'compromise', 252.204-7012(a))
deadline: Start at once; findings feed the 72-hour report
notify: Internal (decision log); results go into the DoD report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FC-4 includes the clause and the company holds CDI. Review of the 2026 CUI spill is POAM-018

obligation: DoD cyber incident report
trigger: Cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the CDI residing in it
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil, with at least the required elements listed there
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FC-4 (CDI held). FC-3 has the clause but no CDI today. Also applies if CUI is found in a mailbox during a BEC
runbook: CUI (and BEC if CUI is involved)

obligation: DoD-approved medium assurance certificate
trigger: Needed to file any DoD cyber incident report
deadline: Have or acquire before an incident; POL-03 4.6 requires two holders at all times
notify: Certificate provider listed at https://public.cyber.mil/eca/
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - gap today: the only certificate expired 2026-05-20 (P03 G-114; POAM-013)

obligation: Submit malicious software to the DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported cyber incident
deadline: With or after the report, as DC3 or the Contracting Officer instructs
notify: DC3 (never the Contracting Officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when malware is isolated

obligation: Preserve images and monitoring data
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident
deadline: Preserve images of all known affected systems and relevant monitoring and packet capture data for at least 90 days from submission of the report
notify: Internal; DoD may request the media or decline interest
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - preserve before any rebuild

obligation: Access for forensic analysis and damage assessment
trigger: DoD requests additional information or equipment, or elects a damage assessment
deadline: On request
notify: DoD; the Contracting Officer requests damage assessment information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Subcontractor gives the DoD incident report number to the prime (inbound)
trigger: A subcontractor holding CDI reports a cyber incident to DoD
deadline: As soon as practicable after the subcontractor reports
notify: The company (FC-4 Project Executive records it)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the A&E subcontract today; for the 14 trades once flowdown is added (POAM-016)

obligation: Cloud service provider meets incident duties for CDI it holds
trigger: Incident at the government-community cloud provider affecting CDI
deadline: The provider complies with paragraphs (c) to (g); the company requires and ensures it
notify: Provider reports to DoD; the company coordinates through the provider incident line in the CRM
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CPE provider

obligation: Report covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment
trigger: Covered equipment or services identified during contract performance, including through notification by a subcontractor
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days of that report
notify: Contracting Officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all four federal contracts. Used for FC-2 on 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-26
runbook: Both (not triggered by BEC or CDI loss alone)

obligation: Correct SAM EFT information and alert the federal paying office
trigger: The company's EFT information in SAM was changed without authorization, or a federal payment is missing
deadline: Immediately. If EFT data was incorrect or revised within 30 days of the Government's release of the payment and the funds have left the payment office, the Government is deemed to have paid and the company must recover the funds
notify: SAM (correct the record); Contracting Officer and paying office for each affected contract
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - federal variant (C) of the BEC runbook

obligation: Pay subcontractors on federal contracts despite a diverted payment
trigger: A payment meant for a subcontractor on a federal job went to an attacker
deadline: Within 7 days of the company's receipt of the Government's payment; interest penalty if late
notify: The subcontractor, after call-back verification of its real bank details
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FC-1 to FC-4

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Unauthorized access to personal information of Florida residents (for example name plus Social Security number, or an email address plus the password that opens the account, 501.171(1)(g))
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; delay only on a law enforcement agency's written request
notify: Each affected Florida resident (mail or email)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a compromised account or system held employee or subcontractor-worker personal information

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to the notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (instead of individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing and keep 5 years; give it to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Only with counsel's agreement

obligation: Vendor (third-party agent) breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (payroll and HR SaaS, benefits administrator) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company no later than 10 days after its determination
notify: The company (General Counsel and HR Director)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - tracked in vendor contracts (STD-03)

obligation: State data breach notification (other states)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of another state (definitions vary)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check: some craft workers and subcontractor employees live outside Florida

obligation: Accuracy of the SPRS score and federal representations after an incident
trigger: An incident shows that SP 800-171 requirements scored as implemented are not met
deadline: Before the next SPRS update, proposal, or representation; counsel decides on any earlier correction
notify: SPRS; Contracting Officer if counsel advises
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company practice to avoid inaccurate representations (False Claims Act exposure, P01 R-008)

obligation: CMMC status currency after an incident
citation: DFARS 252.204-7021(a) ('current': no changes in compliance since the status date) and (d)(1); 32 CFR 170.22
trigger: An incident shows that a requirement of the held CMMC level is no longer met
deadline: Before relying on the status for any award or making the next affirmation; restore compliance first
notify: Internal (CEO as Affirming Official); counsel
applies_at_this_tier: Not yet: no CMMC status is held. Applies after the Level 2 (C3PAO) assessment planned for 2027-04. The final clause has no separate incident notice

obligation: FC-4 Contracting Officer courtesy call
trigger: A DoD report is filed, or an incident affects FC-4 schedule or CUI exchange
deadline: Same day as the DoD report
notify: Army Corps of Engineers Contracting Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company practice; not a separate clause duty
owner: FC-4 Project Executive with General Counsel

obligation: Owner notice of a compromised payment channel
trigger: An owner may have received false remittance instructions from a company mailbox or lookalike domain
deadline: Immediately by phone to the owner's accounts payable contact on file, then in writing
notify: Owner's accounts payable and project representative
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: MBSS and installation client notice
citation: MBSS service agreements and installation contracts (contract)
trigger: Client facility security details or client system credentials may have been accessed
deadline: Per each agreement (most require notice within 72 hours of confirming a security incident)
notify: Client's designated security contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 38 MBSS client sites; installation clients per contract
owner: Director of Technology and Security Systems with General Counsel

obligation: Surety notice
citation: General indemnity agreement with the surety (contract)
trigger: A loss large enough to affect working capital or the ability to pay subcontractors
deadline: Per the agreement
notify: Surety
applies_at_this_tier: Check with counsel - contractual

obligation: Lender and PE sponsor notice
citation: Credit agreement and sponsor reporting terms (contract)
trigger: Material loss or event under the credit agreement
deadline: Per the agreement
notify: Lender agent; PE sponsor's operating partner
applies_at_this_tier: Check with counsel - contractual
owner: Chief Executive Officer; Chief Financial Officer

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a registrant
deadline: Within 4 business days after determining materiality
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: Not applicable: the company is privately held

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties. Default position: the company does not pay
